description.text: The Company was founded by Robert Pera in 2005. We sell equipment, and provide the related software platforms, worldwide through a network of over 100 distributors, on-line retailers and direct to customers through our webstores. Ubiquiti is focused on democratizing network technology on a global scale. Our devices play a role in creating networking infrastructure in over 200 countries and territories around the world. Our professional networking products are powered by our UISP and UniFi OS software platforms to provide high-capacity distributed Internet access and unified information technology management, respectively. We develop technology platforms for high-capacity distributed internet access, unified information for secure and easily managed network infrastructure, connected sensors, cameras, access devices, appliances and other endpoint devices for enterprises, industrial and service-provider environments. We categorize our solutions into two main categories: high performance networking technology for enterprises and service providers. We target the enterprise and service provider markets through our highly engaged community of service providers, distributors, value added resellers, webstores, systems integrators and corporate IT professionals, which we refer to as the Ubiquiti Community.

analysis_md:
# UI — Ubiquiti Inc.
v5 re-run, 2026-10-14 (supersedes the v4 analysis of 2026-10-13; the v4 result is summarized under Thoughts). Price $620.24 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $37,567,936,800 on 60,570,000 diluted shares — inside the <$40B scope. Fiscal year ends June 30; FY2026 ended 2026-06-30, 3.48 months ago (dcf_numbers.json diagnostics), so the latest FY is current, not stale.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, or key_numbers.md — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Designer of networking hardware and the software that runs it: UniFi access points, switches and gateways, Protect cameras, Access door controls and NAS, plus the declining UISP/Service Provider line for broadband ISPs. Enterprise Technology is the bulk of revenue (Q4 FY2026: $868.3M of the $937.3M quarterly total, per the earnings release coverage). The model is deliberately lean: sold through distributors/resellers and a community of installers, no large direct sales force, no per-device licensing fees — enterprise-grade kit at a fraction of Cisco/Fortinet total cost of ownership. Founder/CEO Robert Pera owns ~93% of the shares (per the prior pass's review of 10-K ownership coverage), there are no earnings calls, and the float is tiny — the 52-week range is $500.23–$1,099.99 (Finnhub), so the price signal is noisy by construction.

Latest results (Q4 / FY2026, reported 2026-08-21): Q4 revenue a record $937.3M, +23.5% YoY (earnings release); FY2026 revenue $3,274,162,000, +27.2% YoY (engine rev_yoy_latest 27.22%); GAAP diluted EPS $15.85 for FY2026, $4.70 in Q4 (non-GAAP $4.73, a beat vs $4.03 consensus per MarketBeat). A $1.00/quarter dividend was declared, with an intention to pay at least $1.00/quarter through FY2027, and the $500M buyback authorization was extended to September 2027. No post-FY quarter has reported yet: ttm.py exits non-zero for UI — "no post-FY YTD fact (no 10-Q since the 2026-06-30 fiscal year end)" for OCF, capex, SBC and shares — so TTM = FY2026. Q1 FY2027 earnings are expected around November 6, 2026 (MarketBeat estimate). Analyst FY2027 EPS estimates (~$16.94, Zacks via MarketBeat) sit barely above FY2026's $15.85 GAAP EPS — the Street expects a sharp growth deceleration, which matters for the scenario sanity check below.

## Owner's earnings (SEC EDGAR filing-direct history)
- FY2026 conservative: OCF $928,682,000 − capex $19,738,000 − SBC $7,444,000 = **$901,500,000 = $14.88/share** (base_oe_total_latest_fy and base_oe_latest_per_share, dcf_numbers.json). SBC is trivial next to OCF — the lean, founder-led cost structure is real, not an add-back story.
- FY2026 maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **$587,673,000** (financials_history.csv) — materially lower, and the gap is the flag to understand: ΔNWC was a **+$372,630,000 build** in FY2026 (inventory/receivables to support +27% growth and to stock against component constraints), after NWC *releases* of $192,240,000 (FY2025) and $195,519,000 (FY2024) flattered those years' cash conversion. The conservative figure is the one to use — OCF is actual cash after working capital — but the honest read is that FY2026 cash earnings sit between the two definitions if the WC build persists.
- Earnings quality check: FY2026 net income $960,303,000 vs OCF $928,682,000 — a small gap, no divergence flag, no one-off gain in the base. Operating income rose to $1,185,442,000 from $836,280,000 in FY2025 (financials_history.csv); the OE jump is operating performance, not an accounting artifact.
- History is volatile by construction: OE was negative in FY2023 (−$171,096,000) despite net income of +$407,641,000, because OCF went to −$145,428,000 on a +$526,000,000 working-capital build; OE positive 4 of the last 5 years (dcf_numbers.json). FY2024 revenue was essentially flat ($1,928,490,000 vs $1,940,512,000 in FY2023), then FY2025 revenue $2,573,545,000 and FY2026 $3,274,162,000.
- Balance sheet: long-term debt was paid down from $1,041,381,000 (FY2023) to $669,878,000 (FY2024) to $0 (FY2025); the FY2026 row carries no long-term-debt tag and the engine reports net_debt_latest as null, with cash rebuilt to $522,579,000 at FY2026. Net cash is small next to a $37.57B market cap — a strength, but immaterial to the verdict (no BIG_NET_CASH / HIGH_NET_DEBT flag, correctly).
- Share count: 83,252,000 diluted (2017) → 60,451,000 (2023) → **flat for three years** (60,458,000 / 60,534,000 / 60,570,000; share_cagr +0.07%, no buyback-tailwind or dilution flag). The historic buyback tailwind is exhausted at this price; the renewed $500M authorization is small against the market cap.

**Base used and why (BASE_DIVERGENCE resolution):** the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share) is **$10.246027026134074**, vs latest FY **$14.883605745418524**. I pinned the latest FY as the final base via `--base-oe-ps 14.883605745418524`, declared in judgment.json as a `base_override` (value, source and reason recorded there and in the override registry). The median is the distorted figure: it is anchored on FY2024, a flat-revenue trough year, while FY2026 is corroborated by net income of $960,303,000, clean OCF conversion and record quarterly prints — and ttm.py confirms no post-FY 10-Q exists, so the latest FY *is* the TTM figure. The caveat is priced into the scenarios instead: FY2026 may itself be a Wi-Fi 7 refresh-cycle high, which is why the bear/super-bear OE multipliers (0.90 / 0.75) and a 35% combined bear weight do real work, and why the method range below is reported.

## MOAT: 6/10 — moderate-strong, not wide
Justification: UniFi ecosystem switching costs plus a structural lean cost advantage and proven pricing power, against one-off hardware revenue with no recurring annuity, no white-glove enterprise support, copycat license-free rivals, and extreme founder/key-man concentration.
- FOR: UniFi ecosystem switching costs — once an installer/SMB standardizes on UniFi OS, networking, Protect, Access and NAS are managed in one pane of glass, and ripping it out means replacing the whole stack; structural cost advantage — no direct sales force, no licensing-fee infrastructure, SBC of only $7,444,000 against OCF of $928,682,000 supports high margins while undercutting Cisco/Fortinet total cost of ownership; proven pricing power — operating income rose from $836,280,000 (FY2025) to $1,185,442,000 (FY2026) on the revenue growth; capital discipline — long-term debt eliminated by FY2025, dividend initiated at $1.00/quarter, buybacks executed when the stock was cheap.
- AGAINST: No recurring revenue — one-off hardware, re-won every refresh cycle, no subscription/licensing annuity like the incumbents have; no white-glove enterprise support — a hard ceiling on Fortune 500 penetration, the richest segment; the model is copyable at the low end — TP-Link Omada and others explicitly mimic the license-free playbook; key-man and governance concentration — Pera owns ~93%, is the product visionary, and offers no calls or guidance, and the tiny float manufactures volatility rather than pricing information; East-Asia contract manufacturing and component sourcing — tariff, supply and counterfeit/IP exposure, with Q4 coverage flagging higher component and shipping costs; Service Provider Technology is in decline, so growth is single-engine.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years (dcf_numbers.json cap_years): growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
Inputs: base OE/share $14.883605745418524 (base_override pin = FY2026 = TTM, above), moat 6 (CAP 9.8y), probabilities 10/25/30/25/10, offsets −0.12/−0.05/0/+0.05/+0.12 and OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 — all at the defaults, because the defaults are genuinely calibrated to this company's prints (see sanity check). Price $620.24.

**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** engine blended base growth is 23.07% (g_base; components: rev CAGR 5y 11.52%, rev CAGR 3y 19.04%, latest rev YoY +27.22%, OE/share CAGR 2y 31.17%, share-count adjustment −0.07pp). Against actual prints — FY2026 revenue +27.2% YoY, with FY2026 quarterly revenue YoY prints of roughly +33% (Q1), +18.7% (Q3) and +23.5% (Q4) per earnings coverage — the scenario starts sit inside the observed range, not below it: super-bull 35.07% ≈ the best recent quarters, bear 18.07% ≈ the softest recent quarter (Q3, +18.7%), super-bear 11.07% ≈ the 5-yr revenue CAGR (11.52%). No start needs a deceleration excuse, and none exceeds a print the company has actually made. The opposite failure does not apply either: the blend is not capped (23.07% vs the 35% cap) and its components are revenue-led, not tiny-base artifacts. One caution, written rather than modeled: Street FY2027 EPS estimates (~$16.94 vs FY2026 GAAP $15.85) imply much slower near-term EPS growth than the base-case start — the bear weights are where that risk lives.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | 11.07% | 0.75 | Refresh cycle ends, component costs bite, growth reverts to 5-yr trend on a normalized OE base | $133.99 | 5.48% |
| Bear | 25% | 18.07% | 0.90 | Q3-style deceleration persists, margins give back part of FY2026's gain | $219.11 | 7.50% |
| Base | 30% | 23.07% | 1.00 | Blended growth holds 2 yrs, fades over the 9.8-yr CAP | $303.14 | 9.35% |
| Bull | 25% | 28.07% | 1.10 | FY2026 growth roughly repeats; Wi-Fi 7 / NAS / Access tailwinds extend | $414.38 | 11.54% |
| Super bull | 10% | 35.07% | 1.25 | Best-quarter growth sustained with further OE expansion | $635.82 | 15.24% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $326.30, IV@12% $457.00, IV@10% $605.94, weighted IRR 9.85%** at the $620.24 price (upside at 15%: −47.39%).
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield on the pinned base 2.40%, terminal value 24.36% of IV@15% (the low TV share is the fade doing its job — the problem is the starting price against current OE, not terminal assumptions), scenario spread 4.75x, 3.48 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE (latest FY OE/share $14.88 vs 3-yr median $10.25):** resolved in favour of the latest-FY/TTM base, with reasons above — the median is anchored on the FY2024 flat-revenue trough, and the FY2026 figure is corroborated by net income ($960,303,000), clean OCF conversion and record prints, with no one-off gain found; the pin is declared as a `base_override` in judgment.json (source: FY2026 10-K filing-direct figures via the engine). The residual risk (FY2026 = cyclical peak) is handled by the 0.75/0.90 bear multipliers, not by silently using a stale base. Method range: on the median base at default moat 5, the preliminary v5 run gave weighted IRR 7.33% / IV@15% $207.57 — **Tier D on both bases**, so the base choice moves the value materially but does not change the tier.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD (super-bull IV 4.75x super-bear IV):** real, and structural — a hardware grower whose quarterly growth prints ranged from +18.7% to ~+33% within a single fiscal year has a genuinely wide outcome range. Confidence is therefore **medium**, never high with this flag (make_score also clamps it), and the verdict is sized to the weighted/conservative end, not the bull tail.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD (fired on the preliminary median-base run at 1.65%):** the pinned base lifts the OE yield to 2.40%, but the substance of the flag stands — at $620.24 the valuation rests almost entirely on future growth, which is exactly why even the super-bull scenario (35.07% start, 1.25× OE) only reaches a 15.24% IRR. This fragility is the verdict, not a footnote.
- No other flags fired on the final run: no STALE_FY (FY ended 3.48 months ago; ttm.py confirms no post-FY 10-Q exists, so no TTM adjustment is possible or needed), no NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE (net income $960,303,000 vs OCF $928,682,000 in FY2026), no HIGH_NET_DEBT/BIG_NET_CASH (long-term debt $0 in FY2025 and untagged in FY2026, cash $522,579,000 — small vs the $37.57B cap), no DILUTION/BUYBACK_TAILWIND (share count flat for three years), no SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (hardware OE/capex logic fits; capex is genuinely small at $19,738,000), no DATA_GAP (data_gap empty; SBC, capex, shares and OCF all filed for the last 3 FY).

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is a high-quality business at a price that has already collected the next decade of growth. Even granting the most current base ($14.88), growth at the top of what the company has actually printed (35.07%), *and* a 25% OE uplift on top, the IRR is 15.24% — the super-bull case barely clears Andrew's base hurdle. Every other scenario is 5.48–11.54%.
- The method range is unusually honest here: IV@15% $207.57 (median base, preliminary run) to $326.30 (pinned FY2026 base, final run), Tier D under both. There is no defensible trailing input set that gets UI near 15% at $620.24. The v4 pass (2026-10-13) reached the same place — weighted IRR 9.86%, IV@15% $326, Tier D at $619.56 — so the v5 re-run changes the plumbing (declared base_override, hash-stamped numbers), not the answer.
- **Hurdle-clearing price: ~$326.30** (the weighted IV@15%) clears 15% on the final inputs; roughly **$228–245 with a 25–30% margin of safety** — well inside the stock's own 52-week range ($500.23 low is still far above it, but this float has produced a $1,099.99 high and violent drawdowns before, so a re-entry at those levels is not a fantasy scenario).
- What would change the tier: the Q1 FY2027 10-Q (September quarter, expected ~November 6, 2026) holding >25% growth with the FY2026 working-capital build converting back to cash (maintenance OE converging on the conservative figure), or simply a float-driven drawdown toward the low-$300s. Re-run after that filing.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (= tier by numbers; no override — Tier D on both the normalized-median and pinned-FY2026 bases)
- Confidence: **Medium** (capped by WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD; high confidence in the OE arithmetic and that no trailing base clears the hurdle, medium on the growth path)
- One-liner: Elite lean hardware franchise, moat 6/10 — but at $620.24 the weighted IRR is only 9.85% with IV@15% of $326.30, and even the super-bull case barely clears 15%; it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$326, or ~$235 with a margin of safety.
